tvs.title-bl-seo: Why choose eyelid eyeliner micropigmentation: 3 essential points
tvs.text-bl-seo: Today, many young women choose eyeliner tattooing, and for good reason. The procedure delivers not only an excellent result but also maximum comfort in everyday life. Just imagine: no more drawing lines every day, checking the mirror every hour to make sure your pencil, eyeshadow or mascara hasn't smudged, carrying a makeup bag to keep fixing your line, or wiping pencil marks off your upper eyelids. Semi-permanent eye makeup gives you a natural look and more self-confidence. Whatever you're doing, you can be sure your eyeliner won't let you down. We guarantee your eyes will always look made up, and your gaze will be intense and radiant.
tvs.text-bl-seo-2:
3 reasons to choose eyelid micropigmentation

What makes eyelid tattooing stand out? It offers aesthetic benefits on several levels:

  1. It's genuinely pretty. A fine line, with or without shading, makes your eyes stand out. For day or evening makeup, a little mascara on your lashes is all you need. Semi-permanent eye makeup pairs perfectly with any cosmetics: liquid or powder foundation, concealer, bronzer, powder, primer. You can wear absolutely any kind of makeup and still be sure your tattoo will always look gorgeous.
  2. You'll be able to reshape your eyes and hide minor imperfections. Narrow eyes will look bigger, and close-set eyes will look further apart. Eyeliner tattooing will also mask expression lines, lift a drooping eyelid and hide pigment spots or small scars in the area.
  3. You'll save a significant amount of time, as well as the money you'd otherwise spend on cosmetics.

It's also worth mentioning that the procedure comes in a variety of techniques. You can choose not only classic eyeliner, but also eyeliner with shading of varying intensity, or an upper and lower lash line tattoo. These techniques give you room to experiment. Since the effect lasts up to 2 years, once it fades you can try a different technique for comparison.

What you should know about eyelid micropigmentation

Before booking a micropigmentation appointment, it's important to know a few details about the procedure.

There are some contraindications

These include insulin-dependent diabetes, epilepsy, mental disorders, conjunctivitis, inflammation in the eye area, viral illnesses, pregnancy and breastfeeding. Menstruation is not a contraindication. It's also advisable to reschedule the procedure if you feel unwell or have a fever or high blood pressure.

Weigh the pros and cons of each technique

Classic eyeliner can be any thickness and length, with any angle of the line. The wider the line, the more visible it will be, so you'll always need to wear mascara. Eyeliner with shading doesn't go well with blonde lashes: in that case you'll need to tint them or apply mascara regularly, or opt for lash extensions. With the upper and lower lash line technique, on the other hand, the lashes don't need tinting. The line is barely visible and makes the lashes look longer and darker. However, this technique doesn't hide imperfections the way classic eyeliner and shaded eyeliner do.

Preparing for eye micropigmentation

Before the procedure, thoroughly remove your eye makeup, including eyeshadow and mascara. If you have lash extensions, have them removed the evening before the procedure. This ensures the extension glue doesn't prevent the pigment from reaching every point near your natural lashes. If you wear contact lenses, remember to bring a lens case and solution. Take your lenses out and put them in the case right before the session. Once the procedure is over, you can wear them again. Still, if you can manage with glasses for a few hours, that's much better.

Skin care after the procedure

An eyeliner tattoo doesn't require any special care. Since the skin needs to heal and regenerate on its own, we don't recommend that clients use healing ointments. The one exception may be chlorhexidine or a similar antiseptic, which can be applied to the area during the first two days to protect the skin from infection.
The main aftercare rule is to keep the area protected while the skin heals. Avoid washing with hot water, steaming your skin, and going to the sauna, tanning salon or pool. Any physical contact with the eyes is off-limits: no scratching and no picking at flaking skin.

About touch-ups

A touch-up isn't mandatory after eyelid micropigmentation; it's entirely your decision. A touch-up helps to fix any flaws that may appear as the skin heals, deepen the color of the line, add shading if needed, and change the length and width of the line. But if you're completely happy with the result after the first session, you can skip it. If you're unsure, it's best to consult your artist, who will certainly suggest the best solution.

Permanent eye makeup gives you both comfort and self-confidence. Choose your technique and book your procedure. For our part, the artists at the LBar studio in Bucharest will make sure your dream of a perfect eyelid tattoo at an affordable price comes true.

migx_questions.questions-title: How do I choose the right eye contour tattoo shape?
migx_questions.questions-text: First, decide on the shape, length and thickness of the line you like. Look through the artist's portfolio or browse photos online. Our studio's artists can also help you choose the most suitable eyeliner style based on your preferences and eye shape. Before the procedure, a sketch is drawn, discussed and approved together with you.

migx_questions.questions-title: Is there any risk to my eyesight during eye micropigmentation?
migx_questions.questions-text: No, there is no such risk. The artist stretches and holds the eyelid with their fingers so that, even if the client wanted to blink, they couldn't. So there is no risk of harming the eyes during cosmetic eyelid tattooing.

migx_questions.questions-title: Is eye contour micropigmentation allowed during pregnancy or breastfeeding?
migx_questions.questions-text: The procedure is not recommended for pregnant or breastfeeding women because of the anesthetic used. If you do decide on semi-permanent eyelid makeup, it's better to have it done in the third trimester of pregnancy.
Any possible discomfort is eased with an initial and a secondary anesthetic. The procedure is never performed without it. That's why eyeliner tattooing is considered painless.
